items.followUp: What must be true about the resultant force on a body in translational equilibrium?

rubric.why: Identifies the force condition for equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant (net) force on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant force is zero.

rubric.why: States the resulting condition of motion.
rubric.description: States that the body has no acceleration, so it remains at rest or moves with constant velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acceleration is zero or giving an equivalent motion description.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero.
Therefore, it has no acceleration and remains at rest or moves with constant velocity.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a renewable and a non-renewable energy source.

rubric.why: Defines renewable energy sources by how they are renewed.
rubric.description: States that renewable sources are naturally replenished.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining renewable sources as naturally replenished.

rubric.why: Defines non-renewable energy sources by their limited supply or replenishment.
rubric.description: States that non-renewable sources are finite or are not replenished on a human timescale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining non-renewable sources as finite or not replenished on a human timescale.

modelAnswer: Renewable sources of energy are naturally replenished and can be used repeatedly, for example sunlight and wind.
Non-renewable sources are finite and are not replenished on a human timescale, for example coal and oil.

items.followUp: Two masses of 6 kg and 4 kg are connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley. Find their acceleration and the tension in the string. Take g = 9.8 m/s².

rubric.why: Sets up Newton's second-law equations with a consistent choice of direction for the heavier mass.
rubric.description: For m1 > m2, writes the equations of motion for m1 moving downward and m2 moving upward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct equations with the stated mass ordering.

rubric.why: Combines the equations of motion to obtain the acceleration.
rubric.description: Gives the correct acceleration of the two-mass system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct acceleration expression.

rubric.why: Uses the equations of motion to obtain the string tension.
rubric.description: Gives the correct tension in the string.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct tension expression.

rubric.why: Identifies the directions of motion consistent with the assumed ordering of the masses.
rubric.description: States that the heavier mass moves downward and the lighter mass moves upward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct directions and the stated mass ordering.

modelAnswer: Let the masses be m1 kg and m2 kg, with m1 > m2; m1 moves downward and m2 moves upward.
For m1: weight = m1g N; equation of motion: m1g - T = m1a.
For m2: equation of motion: T - m2g = m2a.
Therefore, acceleration: a = [(m1 - m2)/(m1 + m2)]g m/s².
Substituting into either equation of motion gives tension: T = [2m1m2/(m1 + m2)]g N.
